ken (Runtime): Heads-up — CI soak popped an invariant violation in the continuous batching scheduler. intermittent but shows up under ~2k qps. stack excerpt below.

ken (Runtime): ```
ERROR runtime/scheduler: admission: inconsistent state: acquired but remainingCredits=0
  at runtime/scheduler/admission.go:214 acquireAdmissionCredit
  tokenId=0x7f8a, lane=fast, seq=10234
```

aj (Eng): I saw a similar trace yesterday locally when I ran the concurrency harness. suspect race between preemptive-evict and credit-replenish. can you share the reproduce steps?

leo (Platform): this smells like the liveness vs throughput window we discussed — when a lane flip happens and we reconcile credits we sometimes double-count in-flight requests. quick mitigation: add an invariant check in the admission path + metric so we can detect frequency before patching.

maria (SRE): :eyes: post the failing logs and I'll add ephemeral tracing to staging to catch the sequence. also we should fire an alert if the invariant trips > 10/min.

ken (Runtime): repro is flaky but i have a minimal harness. gist: ```bash
for i in {1..2000}; do run-harness --concurrency 256 --seed $i || echo "seed $i failed" >> failures.log; done
```
log shows request accepted then immediately evicted with: `evict: reason=credit-mismatch, request_id=...` and the admission counter goes negative.

aj (Eng): short-term fix I'd push: make the credit decrement+evict decision atomic (CAS around credits) and add a fast-path metric so we can measure how often we hit the race. long-term: split tokens into two concepts — livenessTokens (prevent starvation) and throughputCredits (for batching economics). that way preemption only touches throughputCredits.

leo (Platform): +1 to splitting concepts. don't want to change semantics in prod without guardrails. plan: add invariant metric (counter + sample trace) that is no-op unless > threshold, ship to staging, run soak, then decide.

maria (SRE): i'll create the alert in ops-pager (threshold 10/min) and enable verbose tracing for staging. who will take the PR?

aj (Eng): i'll own the PR. will add unit tests, a small simulation test for the split-token idea, and a trace-id appended to request logs for easier correlation. aiming to land a staging patch today.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout started: runtime/staging @aj - build #3421

ken (Runtime): thanks — once staging soak is clean let's schedule a short runway before merging to prod. also we should add a benchmark to check cost impact of the two-token model (microbench + 95p latency).

leo (Platform): noted. will draft a short RFC for the token split pattern so other subsystems can adopt consistent invariants.

maria (SRE): ping @aj when the PR is up, i'll wire the alert and check traces during the soak. :thumbsup:
